## {background-color="#0C0C1A"}

::: {.ghost-text}
02
:::

### Your AI is doing a Wally. {.white-serif}

<div class="rule"></div>

**Wally performs sight using memorised cues.**  
[He narrates the world he was trained to expect — not the one in front of him.]{.mid-text}

[Silicon Valley’s multimodal AI does the same thing:]{.mid-text}

::: {.columns .contrast-boxes}
::: {.column .box-dark}
#### WHAT IT CLAIMS
The machine can now see
:::
::: {.column .box-gold}
#### WHAT IT DOES
Converts pixels to words, reasons about words, describes what it expects
:::
:::

::: {.footer-text}
Spotted Ape — Design Strategy
:::

## {background-color="#F2F1EB" .light-slide}

::: {.page-num}
03 / 07
:::

### Language models narrate vision.  
### They don’t experience it. {.dark-serif}

<div class="rule"></div>

::: {.columns .step-flow}
::: {.column .step-card}
#### PIXELS
Visual input enters the system
:::
::: {.column .step-card}
#### TOKENS
Converted to language before any reasoning occurs
:::
::: {.column .step-card .step-card-active}
#### EXPECTED WORLD
The world it was trained to describe — not the one in front of it
:::
:::

*“Relying on linguistic priors” — hallucinating with pre-trained confidence, not seeing.* {.gray-italic}

::: {.footer-text}
Spotted Ape — Design Strategy
:::

## {background-color="#0C0C1A"}

::: {.page-num}
04 / 07
:::

::: {.ghost-text}
30%
:::

### Midjourney knows what beauty looks like. {.white-serif}
### *Not what it means.* {.gold-serif}

<div class="rule"></div>

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="65%"}
**Beautiful ≠ true.**  
[These models have mastered the statistical grammar of what beautiful images look like. They do not know that glass shatters, nor that wine is liquid.]{.mid-text}

*The perception is absent. The vocabulary remains intact.  
Wally knows all the right words for a bar fight.* {.gray-italic}
:::

::: {.column width="35%"}
::: {.metric-box}
### 30%
accuracy on scientific  
visual reasoning tasks
:::
:::
:::

::: {.footer-text}
Spotted Ape — Design Strategy
:::

## {background-color="#F2F1EB" .light-slide}

::: {.page-num}
05 / 07
:::

### Spatial truth collapses.  
### The people who need it most pay the price. {.dark-serif}

<div class="rule"></div>

::: {.columns .cards-container}
::: {.column .content-card}
[01]{.card-num}
#### AI cannot parse space
Spatial relationships — where things are relative to each other — vanish in translation.
:::
::: {.column .content-card}
[02]{.card-num}
#### The wrong people bear the cost
AI-mediated visual description omits precisely the structural info users depend on.
:::
::: {.column .content-card}
[03]{.card-num}
#### Proximity as meaning disappears
The visual grammar of arrangement evaporates in translation. Wally cannot give directions.
:::
:::

::: {.footer-text}
Spotted Ape — Design Strategy
:::

## {background-color="#0C0C1A"}

::: {.page-num}
06 / 07
:::

::: {.ghost-text-wally}
WALLY
:::

### This is not an AI problem. {.white-serif}
### *It is a design problem.* {.gold-serif}

<div class="rule"></div>

::: {.insight-list}
- Organisations route insight through assumption, not proximity — and call it research.
- Expertise without lived experience builds things that are beautiful and wrong.
- You design for the world you expect. Your users inhabit a different one.
:::

::: {.footer-text}
Spotted Ape — Design Strategy
:::

## {background-color="#0C0C1A" .last-slide}

::: {.page-num}
07 / 07
:::

### Stop narrating. {.white-serif}
### *Start perceiving.* {.gold-serif}

<div class="rule"></div>

::: {.imperative-item}
1. **Reason natively in context**  
[Don’t translate lived experience into abstraction before acting on it.]{.mid-text}
:::

::: {.imperative-item}
2. **Proximity is a design method**  
[Build teams structurally close to the problem before generating solutions.]{.mid-text}
:::

::: {.imperative-item}
3. **Design with, not for**  
[The gap between participation and observation is where products fail.]{.mid-text}
:::
